fuente.nota: Texto recortado por párrafos; sin cambios en las frases.

parrafos: Recycling is when you recover scrap or waste and reprocessing the material into useful products. Glass, paper, plastic, and metals such as aluminum and steel are often recycled. Dead plants dead and vegetable scraps can be recycled through composting.
It is important not to confuse recycling with reusing, which is where old things, such as clothes, are donated or given a new use instead of being thrown out.

Most people make about two kilograms of waste (trash) every day, and about 7% of this waste is made up of plastic products that can be recycled. Today, plastic can be recycled into products like picnic tables, park benches, and even high-chairs.

First, plastic is collected and taken to a recycling center, where it is sorted out. When plastic is sorted out by hand, symbols have to be printed on every recyclable plastic product used. Nowadays, machines can sort out the plastic automatically. There are different types of plastic, for example polyethylene, polypropylene, polystyrene, and polyethylene terephthalate. There are two kinds of polyethylene plastic: high density polyethylene (HDPE), and low density polyethylene (LDPE). HDPE plastic is usually used to make milk bottles and bottles for shampoo or detergents. LDPE plastic are usually things like toothpaste tubes, plastic bags, and films for packaging. Polypropylene plastic is used to make buckets, plastic boxes, and flower pots. Polyethylene terephthalate is the material from which water and soft drink bottles are made.

HDPE plastic is ground into a small powder. LDPE plastic, which are usually thin films, need to be ground by a special machine. After that, both plastics are washed with hot water and detergent. Dirt and other things, like labels, are taken off. After the wash, the powder is dried with hot air.

Sometimes, the powder is sold. But other times, the powder is heated, colored, and then put into a pelletizer. The pelletizer makes the powder into little pellets, which are bought by a company that shapes the pellets into pieces of plastic "wood". This plastic wood is used to make flowerpots, trash cans, pipes, picnic tables, benches, toys, mats, and many other things.
resumen_es: Define el reciclaje y lo distingue de la reutilización, y explica paso a paso cómo se recicla el plástico: recogida, clasificación por tipos, triturado, lavado y transformación en granza para fabricar nuevos objetos.
nivel_motivo: El nivel léxico C1 se debe a los nombres de polímeros (polyethylene terephthalate, polypropylene), que son transparentes para un hispanohablante; por lo demás, el texto es breve, descriptivo y de sintaxis sencilla.

ideas_clave.idea: Recycling consists in recovering waste and processing it into new products, and it applies to glass, paper, plastic, metals and, through composting, organic matter.
It should not be confused with reuse, which means giving old items a second life instead of discarding them.
Each person generates about two kilograms of rubbish a day, roughly 7% of it recyclable plastic, which can become furniture such as benches or tables.
Collected plastic is sorted, manually or by machine, into different types, each used for specific products such as bottles, bags or containers.
The plastic is then ground, washed and dried into a powder that is either sold or turned into pellets used to manufacture plastic 'wood' and many other goods.

resumen_modelo: The text explains what recycling is and describes how plastic is recycled. Recycling involves recovering waste such as glass, paper, plastic or metal and turning it into new products, organic waste being composted; it differs from reusing, which gives old objects a new purpose. Since each person produces around two kilograms of waste daily, partly recyclable plastic, the process matters. Plastic is first collected and sorted by type, then ground, washed and dried into a powder, which is either sold or transformed into pellets used to make plastic 'wood' and everyday items.

preguntas.pregunta: Why did recyclable plastic products need printed symbols, and what has changed?
respuestas: When plastic was sorted by hand, symbols were needed so that workers could identify each type; nowadays machines can sort plastic automatically.
preguntas.cita: When plastic is sorted out by hand, symbols have to be printed on every recyclable plastic product used. Nowadays, machines can sort out the plastic automatically.
preguntas.explicacion: Hay que relacionar la clasificación manual con los símbolos y señalar la automatización actual.

preguntas.pregunta: Which type of plastic is usually used to make milk bottles?
preguntas.cita: HDPE plastic is usually used to make milk bottles and bottles for shampoo or detergents.
preguntas.explicacion: Las botellas de leche son de HDPE. El LDPE se usa para bolsas y tubos, el polipropileno para cubos y macetas y el PET para botellas de agua y refrescos.

preguntas.pregunta: What are water and soft drink bottles made of?
preguntas.cita: Polyethylene terephthalate is the material from which water and soft drink bottles are made.
preguntas.explicacion: Son de PET (tereftalato de polietileno). Los demás plásticos se asocian en el texto a otros productos o no se les asigna uso.

preguntas.cita: HDPE plastic is ground into a small powder.
preguntas.explicacion: «Ground» es el participio de «grind» (moler, triturar), no el sustantivo «suelo».

preguntas.explicacion: Se seca con aire caliente, no frío; también el lavado se hace con agua caliente y detergente.

preguntas.pregunta: What can happen to the plastic powder at the end of the process?
respuestas: It can be sold directly, or it can be heated, coloured and made into pellets, which a company then shapes into plastic 'wood' used for products such as benches, pipes or toys.
preguntas.cita: Sometimes, the powder is sold. But other times, the powder is heated, colored, and then put into a pelletizer.
preguntas.explicacion: La respuesta debe recoger las dos salidas posibles: venta del polvo o transformación en granza y luego en «madera» plástica.
